caveats: readBack/finalReadBack fields in the ledger below are ALL BOGUS ([]) — the readEditionFile helper assumed a single-entity GET returns a flat `{properties:[...]}` array (the POST create/append response shape, per the #275 finding), but a GET actually wraps the payload as `{entity:{...}}` with properties KEYED by name (`entity.file`). Confirmed via a read-only scratch check post-run (GET entity/{libraryId}?props=name -> `{entity:{name:[...]}}`). Fixed in the script for future use. NONE of the reported verdicts depend on this helper: the baseline/replace/ambiguous-branch findings all come from (1) the upload POST response bodies, which use the genuinely-flat `properties` array shape and were parsed correctly (validated by successful PUTs against the returned upload.url in steps a and b), and (2) direct property/{id} GETs (the 404 after DELETE). Teardown is independently confirmed clean via fresh GETs on the edition AND work entities (404/404) — entity DELETE removes its properties atomically (established precedent, #321-era probes), so the two live file properties this run created (v2's real upload + v3's metadata-only ignored-_id entry) are gone even though the buggy pre-teardown read never found them to delete individually.
